definition: vLLM is an open-source software framework for inference and serving of large language models and related multimodal models.
details: Originally developed at the University of California, Berkeley's Sky Computing Lab, the project is centered on PagedAttention, a memory-management method for transformer key–value caches, and supports features such as continuous batching, distributed inference, quantization, and OpenAI-compatible APIs.

explainer.lead: How to install vLLM, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Created at UC Berkeley Sky Computing Lab (Woosuk Kwon, Zhuohan Li and others, 2023); now a PyTorch Foundation project.

install.python: pip install vllm   # Linux + NVIDIA/AMD GPU
install.javascript: npm install openai   # talk to vLLM’s OpenAI-compatible server

quickstart.python:
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct")
params = SamplingParams(temperature=0.7, max_tokens=64)
for out in llm.generate(["Explain KV caching in one sentence."], params):
    print(out.outputs[0].text)
# or serve it:  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct

explainer.inAi: High-throughput self-hosted LLM serving thanks to PagedAttention and continuous batching; any OpenAI SDK can call it.

tiers.eli5: It is a serving engine that lets one computer answer many model requests quickly by managing memory neatly instead of wasting it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers deploy models on it with continuous batching and OpenAI-compatible APIs; a common pitfall is that memory savings depend on PagedAttention being used well, and it is built for transformers, whose attention is not permutation-invariant without positional information.
tiers.paperLevel: A framework built around PagedAttention, a memory-management method for transformer key–value caches, supporting continuous batching, distributed inference, quantization, and OpenAI-compatible APIs; it was originally developed at UC Berkeley's Sky Computing Lab.

explainer.example: A team serves a large language model to many users at once, and continuous batching keeps the GPU busy as requests arrive.
